facts.claim: German forces invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France declared war two days later.
Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939. The United States and the Soviet Union entered the war later.
Soviet forces entered eastern Poland on 17 September 1939, after Germany had invaded from the west. This followed the secret protocol of the German-Soviet pact.
The invasion of Poland marked the start of war in Europe. Germany attacked from the west while the Soviet Union later entered eastern Poland under the secret protocol.
Britain and France declared war on 3 September, after Germany invaded Poland on 1 September. Their declaration did not immediately stop the German campaign.
Germany invaded Poland first, on 1 September 1939. Britain and France declared war on 3 September.
Germany, Italy and Japan were the principal Axis powers. Their alliance did not mean that every campaign was planned or conducted jointly.
Operation Barbarossa began on 22 June 1941. It opened the German-Soviet front and violated the 1939 non-aggression pact.
Germany invaded Denmark and Norway in April 1940. The campaign secured routes and strategic positions in northern Europe.
Germany attacked the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg before advancing into France. France signed an armistice in June 1940.
France signed an armistice with Germany in June 1940. The country was divided into occupied and nominally unoccupied zones under the settlement.
German air attacks sought to weaken Britain's air defenses and prepare conditions for a possible invasion. Britain remained in the war after the Luftwaffe failed to secure air superiority.
The German Sixth Army surrendered at Stalingrad in February 1943. The defeat became a major turning point on the Eastern Front.
The Normandy landings began Operation Overlord and opened a major western front in German-occupied France. Allied forces then advanced inland.
The Battle of the Bulge was Germany's last major offensive on the Western Front. Allied forces eventually repelled it.
Soviet forces captured Berlin in the final phase of the European war. Germany's surrender followed in May 1945.
Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941. The United States declared war on Japan the following day.
At Midway, U.S. forces inflicted major losses on Japan's carrier fleet. The battle shifted the initiative in the Pacific toward the Allies.
The Guadalcanal campaign began in August 1942. It was an early sustained Allied offensive in the Pacific.
Allied forces captured selected islands and bypassed others to build forward bases. This strategy brought them closer to Japan while limiting some costly assaults.
Japan had been at war in China since 1937. The Pacific war widened when Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in 1941.
The Battle of the Coral Sea checked the Japanese operation against Port Moresby. It was a carrier battle in which opposing fleets did not directly sight one another.
U.S. forces captured Iwo Jima after intense fighting in 1945. Its airfields were strategically valuable for operations nearer Japan.
Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941, Midway was fought in June 1942, and Iwo Jima in 1945. The sequence shows the widening and later Allied advance of the Pacific war.
The Allied victory at El Alamein in late 1942 halted the Axis advance in Egypt. It helped shift the balance in North Africa.
The German surrender at Stalingrad in February 1943 marked a major reversal on the Eastern Front. Soviet forces thereafter advanced westward over time.
Midway inflicted heavy losses on Japan's carrier forces. It helped turn the Pacific conflict from Japanese expansion toward sustained Allied advances.
The Normandy landings opened a large Allied front in western Europe. They placed pressure on German forces from the west while Soviet forces advanced from the east.
After the Normandy landings, Germany faced a major Allied offensive in the west while Soviet forces advanced in the east. The two-front pressure narrowed Germany's room to maneuver.
El Alamein was fought in 1942, Stalingrad ended in February 1943, and the Normandy landings began in June 1944. These events marked shifts in several theatres.
Roosevelt and Churchill issued the Atlantic Charter in August 1941. It outlined broad principles for the post-war order, although it was not a treaty.
At Casablanca in January 1943, Roosevelt and Churchill announced the policy of unconditional surrender. The Soviet Union was not represented at that meeting.
The Tehran Conference in late 1943 was the first wartime meeting of Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin. They discussed coordination against Germany and the opening of a western front.
At Yalta, the Allied leaders discussed Germany's occupation and the emerging post-war settlement. The final division into occupation zones was implemented after Germany's defeat.
The Potsdam Conference met in July and August 1945 after Germany's surrender. The Allied leaders addressed occupation policy and post-war arrangements.
Lend-Lease enabled the United States to provide military supplies to countries whose defense it considered vital. It preceded U.S. entry into the war.
Stalin represented the Soviet Union at both conferences. Roosevelt represented the United States and Churchill represented Britain.
Nazi officials at Wannsee coordinated the implementation of the mass murder of European Jews. The genocide had already begun in occupied territories before the meeting.
The Holocaust was the systematic persecution and murder of six million European Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators. Other groups were also persecuted and murdered by the Nazi regime.
Nazi authorities forcibly concentrated Jewish residents in ghettos under conditions of deprivation and violence. Many people were later deported to killing centers or murdered locally.
Auschwitz-Birkenau was a complex of concentration and killing camps in occupied Poland. It became one of the principal sites of the Holocaust.
Nazi officials used “Final Solution” as a euphemism for the genocide of Europe's Jews. The phrase concealed a policy of systematic mass murder.

The Holocaust was a state-organised genocide during the Nazi era, carried out across Europe by Germany and collaborators. It unfolded through persecution, deportation, mass shootings and killing centers.
Jewish resistance fighters began the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising in April 1943 when German forces moved to deport the remaining residents. German forces suppressed the revolt.
The Polish Home Army began the Warsaw Uprising in August 1944. It was a separate event from the 1943 Warsaw Ghetto Uprising.
Resistance groups in France gathered intelligence, circulated information and carried out sabotage. Their actions supported the Allied campaign but varied across networks and regions.
British codebreakers at Bletchley Park helped decipher German Enigma communications. This intelligence contributed to Allied planning and convoy protection.
Governments rationed food and other goods because wartime demand and disruption created shortages. The specific systems differed across countries.
Resistance took many forms, from armed struggle to intelligence and civilian support. Its organisation and influence differed by country and period.
The Allies landed in Normandy in June 1944 and liberated Paris in August. They continued their advance toward Germany afterward.
Germany signed an unconditional surrender at Reims on 7 May 1945. A further signing took place in Berlin the next day.
Germany's surrender took effect on 8 May 1945 in western Europe. The Soviet Union marked the end of the European war on 9 May because of the timing of the Berlin signing.
Germany signed at Reims on 7 May and a further instrument in Berlin on 8 May 1945. Different surrender ceremonies reflected the Allied coalition and the Eastern Front.
The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945. Nagasaki was bombed three days later.
The second atomic bomb was dropped on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945. Japan announced its acceptance of surrender terms later that month.
Japan formally signed the surrender instrument on 2 September 1945 aboard the USS Missouri. The announcement of acceptance had been made in August.

Germany surrendered in May 1945, the atomic bombs were dropped in August, and Japan signed the surrender in September. The sequence distinguishes the end of the European war from the formal end of the global conflict.
War and persecution displaced millions of people across Europe. Many survivors could not or did not return to their former homes after the conflict.
After Germany's defeat, Allied powers occupied and administered the country. The longer-term division and post-war institutions are covered in CP011.
The war involved connected campaigns across several continents and oceans. Germany's 1940 armistice with France did not end the wider conflict.
